title: a record read answered by an authoritative CNAME to a name outside the zone reads as a measured absence -- hosted DMARC published by CNAME reads as 'NO _dmarc record', and a DKIM selector declared TXT and published as a CNAME as a HALF PAIR
body:
FOUND 2026-10-14 by critic-shell in its review of 0193's build, carried by cc in 0193's commit draft as found in passing, and filed by vc. Read in the code by vc at main 22b25562, whose lib/ is 99dd3106's; not driven. WHAT HAPPENS: - A record read asks the domain's own nameserver, and from 0193 asks it without recursion (infra_dns_read). When the asked name is a CNAME to a name outside the zone, an authoritative server answers with the CNAME row alone, with AA set, and does not chase the target: it is not authoritative for it, and it was asked not to recurse. - _idns_rows keeps only rows of the asked type (lib/infra.dns:155-164 at 99dd3106), so the CNAME row is dropped and the read returns rc 0 with no row: a measured absence. - check: an empty `_dmarc` read under a declared policy is drift, "profile declares `policy:

` and there is NO _dmarc record" (lib/infra.check:185-187 at 99dd3106). So DMARC hosted by a provider and published as `_dmarc. CNAME ` reads as missing. A DKIM selector the profile declares as TXT (lib/infra.check:291) and the domain publishes as a CNAME to the sender's key reads as missing too, so a HALF PAIR. A profile declaring `dmarc: none` never reads `_dmarc`, so it is not affected. - init reads `_dmarc` through the same reader (lib/infra.init:174), so it records no DMARC for such a domain. - It predates 0193 wherever the nameserver does not recurse, which is nearly everywhere. 0193 makes it everywhere. WHAT A FIX MUST DO (cc builds it and vc reviews it): - A read whose authoritative answer holds a CNAME for the asked name and no row of the asked type is never a measured absence. Either it follows the CNAME, reading the target from its own zone's nameserver under the same rule (without recursion, measured only on AA) to a bounded depth, or it reports the read NOT MEASURED, naming the CNAME's target. The builder chooses and says why. Following is how every resolver sees the record, and every receiver that checks DMARC. - The rule lives in the one reader, so every read gets it: `_dmarc`, DKIM selectors declared TXT, SPF, and the wildcard RRsets. - A followed record's ttl is the target's, and the row says it was followed. - Arms: a `_dmarc` CNAME to a name outside the zone under a declared policy reads the target's record, or is NOT MEASURED naming the target, never "NO _dmarc record"; the same for a DKIM selector declared TXT; a CNAME whose target cannot be read is NOT MEASURED; a CNAME inside the zone, answered with its target's rows, reads as it does today. Red first on main, green under BSD and GNU. - Pages: lib/pages/infra.md, under "What check reads". It ships in the next release, with everything open. ## Resolution Landed at 7842c4b1 on a green full suite (vc's, 2342 of 2342 ok, 0 not ok, 5 skipped, .errors empty, seal 20261016-1014). - **A read answered by a CNAME and no record of the type asked is NOT MEASURED, never a measured absence.** infra_dns_read gives it its own outcome, with one line naming the asked name and the target, told apart from a reply without AA where it arises, so it sends no interception probe. Every read that goes through the reader gets it: `_dmarc`, a DKIM selector declared TXT, SPF and MX. So DMARC a provider hosts by CNAME is NOT MEASURED, not "NO _dmarc record", and a DKIM key declared TXT and published as a CNAME is NOT MEASURED, not a HALF PAIR. - **A CNAME inside the zone, answered with its target's records, reads as before.** - **The wildcard is the exception**: its profile entry declares the zone's own record at `*.`, so a CNAME there reads as none of the type and is judged as the CNAME it is, as before. - **init records it under `unreviewed:`**, in check's words, and proposes nothing about that facet. - **Following a CNAME is not built** (vc's ruling): it would need the target's zone found through the machine's resolver. The infra page says so. - **Arms:** five, the out-of-zone three red first on main, the in-zone and wildcard-value two holding what main does, all green under BSD and GNU. Declared: - following is not built, and becomes an issue only if a domain of hv's publishes DMARC or a DKIM key by CNAME; - a CNAME inside the zone whose target has no record of the type reads NOT MEASURED rather than as the absence it is; - for a chain of CNAMEs the line names the first hop, not the end of the chain.
